What? No. No, of course not. Why would you even ask me something like that? I mean, I know why, because my family probably called ahead and told you I'm crazy or losing my mind or something, but I don't hear voices or see ghosts or whatever it is you're implying. My eyes and ears work perfectly fine, just like anybody else's. I don't see things that aren't there. I see exactly what *is* there. I mean, I don't have a fancy college degree or anything, I didn't even finish ninth grade, but I'm not stupid and I'm not crazy. I don't have hallucinations. 

If I hear something, it's because someone actually said it out loud. Like when I hear them whispering in the hallway or talking low in the kitchen, I'm hearing real words from real people, not something made up in my head. And my vision is fine. I don't see imaginary things floating around. I see the real bank papers they shove at me, I see the real way they look at each other when I walk into a room. It just really upsets me, honestly, it makes me so mad that they would drag me down here and have a doctor ask me questions like I'm some kind of lunatic who sees things that don't exist. 

I don't. I just pay attention. I have nothing else to do all day since I don't work, so I just watch and I listen. So no, I have never seen or heard anything that other people couldn't see or hear. If I see it, it's because it's right there in the real world, and if they say they don't see it or hear it, well, that's just because they're lying to cover their tracks, not because my eyes are playing tricks on me. I've always had perfect vision, never even needed glasses, so I know exactly what I'm looking at.

No, absolutely not. My memory is perfect. I mean, I just told you, didn't I? I remember exactly what happened last Tuesday, I remember the exact day I figured out what they were doing with the bank statements. I can remember conversations word for word. Like, just the other day, my sister was standing in the hallway, right by the thermostat—she always messes with the thermostat, by the way, turns it down so it's freezing—and she said, "Oh, we don't know where that receipt went." I remember the exact tone of her voice, that fake innocent tone she uses when she thinks she's pulling one over on me. 

My thinking is completely sharp. It has to be, right? If my thinking was messed up, I wouldn't have been able to put all the pieces together. I wouldn't have noticed that the deposits from the church fundraiser didn't match the withdrawals they were making for "household expenses." Who spends four hundred dollars on groceries in three days? Nobody, that's who. I did the math. I sat down at the kitchen table with a calculator and a notepad, and I went through every single line item. Does that sound like someone who has problems with their thinking? 

It's actually really insulting that you would even ask that. It's like you're trying to find a loophole. Well, if you want to know exactly when I figured it all out, you have to understand the timeline of everything. It wasn't just some random day where I woke up and decided to be suspicious. There was a very specific trigger, a very specific moment when things started to shift.

Unusual fixed beliefs? Listen to yourself, doctor. You make it sound like I believe in aliens or ghosts or something. It's not a "belief," and it's definitely not unusual to want your own money to stay where it belongs. It's just the truth. 

The only reason I'm even sitting in this chair right now, the only reason I came in here today, is because my family and my friends—people who are supposed to have my back, mind you—they keep waving these bank papers in my face. They print out these little summaries and they point at the numbers and they say, "Look, look, the math adds up, the bank papers prove nothing was taken!" Like I'm stupid or something. Like I can't see right through what they're doing. 

I don't have any other "beliefs" because I'm too busy dealing with this one massive reality. For over a year now, I've known they're hiding my money. I've known it, and I've watched them do it. They're getting really crafty about how they do it, too. They think they can just shuffle things around and I won't notice the patterns. They use the regular household bills, right? They inflate the electric bill, or they say the water bill was extra high this month, and they funnel it out that way. And then there's the church fundraisers I mentioned before—they use those to siphon it off, pretending it's a donation. And don't even get me started on these sudden trip plans. Oh yeah, my sister is suddenly talking about planning this big weekend getaway, and I'm sitting there thinking, "With whose money? Where is that money coming from all of a sudden?" 

They use all of it—the bills, the fundraisers, the fake trip plans—just to cover up the fact that they are taking what's mine. They think if they create enough paperwork, I'll just get confused and give up. But I won't. I have to keep confronting them. I have to wake up every single day and get right in their faces about the receipts and the deposits, and I will keep doing it. I will keep pushing and asking questions and demanding answers until they finally crack and tell the truth. At first, I thought, okay, maybe things are just tight and they're stressed, maybe they're just bad at budgeting. But then I started really looking. I started tracking every penny. And I realized it wasn't just bad budgeting. It was deliberate. \n\nSo, yes, it's been going on for a year and two months. Fourteen long months of me having to watch my back, having to double-check every piece of mail, every bank statement, every grocery receipt they bring into this house. Fourteen months of them thinking I'm stupid enough to just let it happen because I don't have as much money coming in as I used to. They probably thought, \"Oh, she's stressed about her income dropping, she won't even notice if we skim a little off the top, she'll just blame it on her financial situation.\" \n\nBut they underestimated me. They completely underestimated how closely I pay attention. I mean, a year and two months is a long time to keep up a lie, and they're getting sloppy. But I'm not. I've been onto them since the very beginning, since the day my income changed. I haven't let my guard down for a single second in all these months, and I'm not going to start now.\n\nDoctor: Do you have any other unusual fixed beliefs besides the money being hidden or stolen?\n\nPatient: Unusual fixed beliefs? Listen to yourself, doctor. You make it sound like I believe in aliens or ghosts or something. It's not a \"belief,\" and it's definitely not unusual to want your own money to stay where it belongs. It's just the truth. \n\nThe only reason I'm even sitting in this chair right now, the only reason I came in here today, is because my family and my friends—people who are supposed to have my back, mind you—they keep waving these bank papers in my face. They print out these little summaries and they point at the numbers and they say, \"Look, look, the math adds up, the bank papers prove nothing was taken!\" Like I'm stupid or something. Like I can't see right through what they're doing. \n\nI don't have any other \"beliefs\" because I'm too busy dealing with this one massive reality. For over a year now, I've known they're hiding my money. I've known it, and I've watched them do it. They're getting really crafty about how they do it, too. They think they can just shuffle things around and I won't notice the patterns. They use the regular household bills, right? They inflate the electric bill, or they say the water bill was extra high this month, and they funnel it out that way. And then there's the church fundraisers I mentioned before—they use those to siphon it off, pretending it's a donation. And don't even get me started on these sudden trip plans. Oh yeah, my sister is suddenly talking about planning this big weekend getaway, and I'm sitting there thinking, \"With whose money? Where is that money coming from all of a sudden?\" \n\nThey use all of it—the bills, the fundraisers, the fake trip plans—just to cover up the fact that they are taking what's mine. They think if they create enough paperwork, I'll just get confused and give up. But I won't. I have to keep confronting them. I have to wake up every single day and get right in their faces about the receipts and the deposits, and I will keep doing it. I will keep pushing and asking questions and demanding answers until they finally crack and tell the truth. They want me to just shut up and accept their little bank papers, but I won't let them get away with it.\n\nDoctor: In the past year, have you had a time when you felt very depressed or lost interest in things for at least two weeks?\n\nPatient: Depressed? No. I mean, who has the time to just sit around and be depressed for two whole weeks? Not me, that's for sure. If I just gave up and lost interest in things, like you're saying, they would have completely cleaned me out by now. You think I can just pull the covers over my head and cry? No way. I have to be on top of everything, every single day. \n\nI mean, sure, it makes me mad. It makes me really, really angry when my own sister looks me in the eye and lies about a grocery run, or when they act like I'm the crazy one for asking to see the actual paper water bill instead of just taking their word for it. It's frustrating, you know? It gets my blood boiling. I get stressed out because I'm the only one in that house who actually cares about the truth. But angry isn't depressed. Depressed means you don't care anymore, right? Like you just want to sleep and you lose interest in what's going on around you. \n\nWell, my interest is at an all-time high. If I was depressed, I wouldn't be doing all that. I wouldn't have the energy. I'd just be letting them win and letting them take whatever they want. So no, I haven't been depressed at all. I've never been in any kind of psychiatric hospital, not once in my entire twenty-eight years on this earth. I fold my clothes the same way, I keep my personal papers stacked up exactly where I left them. Everything is where it belongs. \n\nAnd I get out of the house just fine, too. Better than fine, actually. They're exactly what's keeping me from letting them get away with this.\n\nDoctor: About how long have you been convinced that your family is taking or hiding your money?\n\nPatient: Well, if you want to know exactly when I figured it all out, you have to understand the timeline of everything. Not until I started demanding to see the actual utility bills and the bank statements. It’s funny how that works, isn't it? The second you start catching people in their lies, the second you don't let them just walk all over you, suddenly they want to lock you up and call you crazy. But I have a completely clean record. No mental health problems, ever. And they know that. They're just grasping at straws because they know I'm onto them and I'm not backing down.\n\nDoctor: Have you noticed any trouble keeping up with your daily activities, work, or relationships since this started?\n\nPatient: Trouble? No. No, I don't have any trouble keeping up with my day-to-day stuff. I mean, yeah, obviously the relationships part is... well, it's strained. We argue. We argue all the time, pretty much every day. My room is completely organized. I know where every single item I own is placed. I mean, I have to, right? Because if I don't keep my things in perfect order, how am I going to know if they’ve been in there digging through my stuff while I’m in the bathroom? So I keep everything tight. I fold my clothes the same way, I keep my personal papers stacked up exactly where I left them. Everything is where it belongs. \n\nAnd I get out of the house just fine, too. I still get myself down to the county clinic whenever I need to go. I walk down to the stop, I take the bus, I get there early, I sign in. I don't need anyone holding my hand. Same thing with my assistance appointments. I never, ever miss an assistance appointment. I make sure I have my folder, I sit in the waiting room, I talk to the people I need to talk to... I do everything I'm supposed to do. I have to stay on top of all that, you know? I have to make sure my assistance paperwork is completely by the book so the county knows I'm responsible, especially with my family trying to pull the wool over everyone's eyes and mess with my accounts. \n\nSo no, I'm not falling behind on anything. I'm handling my life perfectly fine. I don't have a job to go to, but my job right now is keeping track of what's mine, and I work very hard at it. Probably more tired, to be perfectly honest with you, with all the stress they put me through every single day. I don't have anything like that going on. \n\nMy thoughts are my own thoughts. Nobody is putting anything inside my head. Nobody can control what you think. \n\nAnd controlling my body? I walk exactly where I want to walk. Like, bouncing off the walls or something? No, definitely not. And I definitely don't need less sleep. I need my sleep, I really do. They'd love it if I was too tired to notice what they were doing. \n\nSo I make sure I get my rest. I go into my room right around ten o'clock every single night, I make sure the door is locked tight, I double-check that my purse is tucked away in the back of my closet where nobody can get a hand on it, and I go to sleep. I don't have that kind of extra energy at all. \n\nHonestly, keeping track of everything they're doing... it wears me out. So no, I'm not running around with all this extra energy, and I definitely am not skipping out on my sleep. I get tired just like anybody else. Probably more tired, to be perfectly honest with you, with all the stress they put me through every single day.
